title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the analytic modular family of elliptic curves over the upper half-plane D^+ (X_{D^+} = (D^+ × C)/Z^2), rigidified by a 'strict Torelli' rigidification, i.e. an oriented basis of H_1. Because this rigidification is given by a basis of H_1, the group SL(2,Z) acts naturally on the right, by change of basis. The previous page wrote this action as τ∘g = (dτ+b)/(cτ+a) for g = (a b; c d).

Step 1 (this page). Since g^{-1} = (d −b; −c a), the same rule gives (11): τ∘g^{-1} = (aτ−b)/(−cτ+d).

Step 2. He introduces τ_∞ = diag(−1, +1) in GL(2,Z). Conjugation by τ_∞ changes the signs of the off-diagonal entries: τ_∞(A B; C D)τ_∞^{-1} = (A −B; −C D). Hence τ_∞(g^{-1}) = (d b; c a), which he describes as 'exchange of a and d'.

Step 3. Plugging this into the right action gives (13): τ∘τ_∞(g^{-1}) = (aτ+b)/(cτ+d), the usual Möbius action.

Step 4. The map g ↦ τ_∞(g^{-1}) is an anti-automorphism of SL(2,Z): inversion composed with an outer automorphism. It therefore turns the natural right action into a left action. He declares that from now on SL(2,Z) acts on D^+ by (13). He notes this is not the most evident 'modular' action, since the natural one comes from the Torelli problem on the right, but it is the one consecrated by usage.

What follows. The next page lifts this to an action of the semidirect product Z^2·SL(2,Z) on D^+ × C, T_{g,m,n}(τ,z) = (gτ, z/(cτ+d) + m + n gτ). It then states that X_{D^+} → D^+ is a universal covering of M_{1,1} with automorphism group SL(2,Z).

Purpose: a careful bookkeeping of left/right conventions, to reconcile the intrinsic (moduli-theoretic) action with the classical one. The choice of the notation τ_∞ for diag(−1,1) is suggestive: it is the matrix of complex conjugation (the Frobenius at the infinite place) acting on H_1 of a real elliptic curve with a suitable basis. That fits Grothendieck's Galois-theoretic outlook on M_{1,1}.
errors: No mathematical errors. Formulas (11), (12) and (13) all check against the convention τ∘g = (dτ+b)/(cτ+a) of the previous page.
Minor terminological point: g ↦ τ_∞(g^{-1}) is an anti-automorphism, not a homomorphism. The garbled word is probably 'anti(auto)morphisme', which would be correct.

ideas.what: Converting the natural right action of SL(2,Z) on D^+ (from change of H_1-basis) into the standard left Möbius action via the anti-automorphism g ↦ τ_∞ g^{-1} τ_∞^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: left/right action conventions for the modular group; transpose/inverse anti-automorphisms

ideas.what: Naming diag(−1,1) in GL(2,Z) as τ_∞, i.e. complex conjugation acting on the lattice/H_1, and using conjugation by it as an outer automorphism of SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: action of complex conjugation (Frobenius at ∞) on the Teichmüller/modular group; real structure on M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (e.g. in work on real elliptic curves and the action of Gal(C/R) on profinite fundamental groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Galois action on π_1 of moduli spaces in general terms; this specific notation is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Purely conventional bookkeeping of left versus right actions of SL(2,Z) on the upper half-plane. It is correct and carefully motivated, but routine. The τ_∞ notation hints at a Galois (complex conjugation) viewpoint, but nothing new is developed on this page.
transcription_corrections: First line: the opening word(s) before 'que' are illegible; likely 'en notant que' or 'on note que', not literally 'on que'.
'l'a[?] morphisme [?]' is probably 'l'anti(auto)morphisme', i.e. the anti-automorphism g ↦ τ_∞(g^{-1}).
In (12) the annotation reads "échange de a et de d" (the transcription's [?] is unnecessary).
The small matrix (a b; c d) at the bottom is written under g as a gloss: g = (a b; c d).
